transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Ethan, Priya, Zoe (Redwood); Aisha, Markus, Derek, Hannah (Citrine)

Summary:
Quick scoping for a 4-week POC focused on latency & throughput SLOs. Primary acceptance criteria: TTFT and TPOT targets at p95/p99 with an explicit sampling plan and orchestration steps for measurement. Discussed workload sizing, cold vs warm KV cache effects, quantized model trade-offs, and measurement harness orchestration. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics covered: SLO definitions (TTFT vs TPOT), sampling strategy, synthetic vs production traffic, warmup/priming, data collection signals, success criteria thresholds, fallback policies, and logistics for hosted vs dedicated pilot.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ethan: all right folks thanks for joining, uh everybody on the Citrine side?
[00:04] Aisha: yeah hi thanks, excited to get this scoped out, we've been trying to lock down realistic latencies across our question-answering pipeline.
[00:10] Priya: awesome, quick intro — Priya Nair, solutions engineer at Redwood, I will run the bench and help interpret the TTFT/TPOT numbers.
[00:16] Markus: Markus here, infra lead, i'll be enabling VPC peering when needed.
[00:19] Derek: and Derek product — success criteria are tied to end user satisfaction, but we'll lean on the SLOs you define.
[00:25] Ethan: perfect. so goal of today is to agree on SLO definition and measurement plan for the POC. specifically TTFT (time to first token) vs TPOT (total per-token time), p95/p99 targets, and how we actually measure them end-to-end.
[00:35] Hannah: also security check — we need KMS integration notes and audit log detail before any private pilot.
[00:40] Zoe: we'll send the SOC2 and KMS notes after this call.

[00:45] Priya: to start, can we get a rough traffic profile? average qps, peak concurrency, typical prompt length, batching needs?
[00:52] Aisha: right now our internal test shows average qps ~12, bursts up to 120 for short windows. median prompt ~150 tokens, 95th ~450 tokens. we plan to start with low conc for POC but want to prove scaling.
[01:05] Priya: got it. so for POC we'll emulate that histogram — steady state 12 qps, bursts to 120. we'll also run a low-latency small prompt set to characterize TTFT.

[01:15] Ethan: quick definitions to align: TTFT is measured from request ingress (Redwood API front door) to when first token bytes hit the client. TPOT we'll capture as per-token average over generation window or total generation latency normalized per token? we typically report both total generation latency and tokens/sec — for SLOs we recommend p95 TTFT and p95 TPOT as primary.

[01:35] Derek: why p95 and p99 both? are we asking for both to be part of acceptance?
[01:40] Priya: yes we propose p95 as the operational SLO and p99 as a guardrail for tail behavior. acceptance requires p95 inside threshold and p99 not exceeding a hard cap. example: for Citrine's small chat model we might propose TTFT p95 <= 250ms, TTFT p99 <= 700ms; TPOT p95 <= 8ms/token and TPOT p99 <= 30ms/token. these are starting points — we'll tune after baseline runs.
[02:10] Aisha: that p95 TPOT 8ms/token — is that optimistic? our current infra has about 12-15ms/token on older infra.
[02:18] Priya: totally depends on model/quantization/hardware and batching. on A100-class we'll see lower per-token for bigger models; quantized int8 can reduce cost but may add some latency variance. POC will run three profiles: unquantized hosted, quantized hosted, and dedicated reserved.

[02:35] Markus: about warm cache: our production load will have a lot of prefix reuse. how do you plan to account for cold-start vs warm cache?
[02:41] Priya: good question — measurement plan includes three phases: cold baseline (empty KV cache), warm steady-state (after priming with representative prompts), and burst simulation with cold-to-warm transitions. we'll report TTFT/TPOT for each phase and weight them according to your traffic histogram.

[02:58] Ethan: important detail — we need to capture network egress latency in Citrine's VPC peering case. Markus, can you confirm whether traffic will go through our public endpoint or via private peering?
[03:07] Markus: for the private pilot we can set up VPC peering; there may be an extra 5-15ms egress depending on routing, we will measure that separately.

[03:15] Hannah: about encryption and KMS: we'd like to validate key wrapping and that logs don't contain PII; send us the audit log fields and retention options.
[03:22] Zoe: will do after the call, plus a short doc on KMS integration steps.

[03:28] Derek: sampling strategy — do we test on synthetic prompts or shared production examples?
[03:32] Priya: both. synthetic allows controlled concurrency sweeps; production-like prompts measure real token distributions and KV cache warmup characteristics. for acceptance we'll prioritize production-like metrics but synthetic tests will help isolate the infra variables.

[03:46] Priya: on orchestration: Redwood will provide a benchmark harness (k6 + custom client) that can drive the API at desired qps with concurrent streams and capture per-request TTFT + per-token timing. harness will also emit GPU metrics hooks via Prometheus endpoints if we run dedicated hosts.
[03:58] Aisha: can we run the harness from our environment too? to include egress effects?
[04:02] Priya: yes, we'll provide the runner as a container and a small runner config guide. you can run from your test VPC.

[04:10] Ethan: acceptance criteria proposal — example concrete charter for POC: take a 200-sample prompt set representative of your worst 95th percentile, run three profiles, report TTFT p95/p99 and TPOT p95/p99, and then run two 30-minute steady-state ramps at expected qps, plus a 10-minute burst test at 2x peak. acceptance = TTFT p95 <= 300ms and TPOT p95 <= 12ms/token, and p99 not exceeding 2x p95 caps. does that feel reasonable?
[04:40] Aisha: the 300ms TTFT p95 is acceptable as long as the p99 guardrail is enforced. we want to minimize tail spikes.

[04:48] Markus: on the dedicated hosts — what's the autoscaling/burst model for dedicated? we might need to see how queueing affects TTFT.
[04:54] Priya: dedicated pools have configurable autoscale and a burst buffer; during POC we'll pin a modest pool and simulate oversubscription to observe queuing effects. we'll measure queue wait times and include that in the TTFT breakdown.

[05:08] Derek: what observability will we get? token-level traces? request attribution?
[05:12] Zoe: console will show per-route cost and latency breakdown, and we'll provide traces for sampled requests showing scheduling, kernel time, and network egress. logs are GDPR-safe and can be disabled for sensitive tests.

[05:24] Priya: one more nuance — when we report TPOT we will include generation time excluding initial tokenizer overhead or include it? we prefer to include end-to-end logic (tokenize + model + network until last token), but break out tokenizer overhead as separate metric.
[05:38] Aisha: prefer end-to-end numbers for acceptance.

[05:42] Ethan: ok wrapping up — timeline: Citi rine shares prompt set and histogram by Tue, 2026-12-21; Redwood runs initial baseline and shares results 2026-12-23; follow-up review 2026-12-23 or 24.

[05:55] Priya: final notes on risks: quantized variants can shift distribution and sometimes affect tail latency; fallback policy should route to unquantized in case of errors but we need to quantify cost delta. we'll include cost per 1k tokens estimates per profile.
[06:12] Hannah: noted, also we need an audit of any PII leakage during logs — please confirm scrub rules.
[06:18] Zoe: will include scrub rules and sample log schema.

[06:22] Ethan: ok thanks everyone, we'll capture action items in the follow-up email and share the harness link.
[06:28] Aisha: thanks all.

[06:30] (call ends)

Notes on measurement plan (embedded in transcript):
- Bench phases: cold baseline, warm steady-state, burst stress.
- Metrics collected: TTFT p50/p95/p99, total generation latency p50/p95/p99, TPOT p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, queue wait time, network egress latency.
- Sampling: collect full traces for 1% of requests and aggregated histograms for all; sample selection seeded to include long prompts.
- Orchestration: runner supports VPC-local execution, Prometheus scraping for dedicated nodes, and CSV output for ingestion into Citrine's metrics system.
- Acceptance: p95 inside threshold + p99 guardrail; if p95 is met but p99 > hard cap, require mitigation plan (e.g., higher model concurrency, smaller batch sizing, different quantization).
